correctness.rationale: For every prime power \(q\ge2\) and \(m\ge2\), explicit singleton-zero evaluation points recover each coefficient, proving injectivity. Additive-character orthogonality gives the exact \(N_r\) count; disjoint exactly-one-zero and all-nonzero strata give precisely \(w_r\). Exhaustive independent direct evaluation of all coefficient vectors over GF(2), GF(3), GF(4), GF(5), GF(7), and GF(8), in 19 dimension/field pairs, matches all multiplicities; coefficient counts sum to \(q^m\). The adjacent-difference formula establishes all collisions and boundary cases. Finite enumeration supports but is not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: For a natural entire prime-power field and dimension family, the code is already of coding-theoretic interest through its GHWs; this theorem supplies all individual-word weight multiplicities, which GHWs alone cannot supply. The result gives a two-tier collision law, exact minimum-word multiplicity and the full Hamming enumerator in closed form, usable directly for the dual MacWilliams enumerator and error detection calculations. Unlike a finite census or textbook change of notation, the claimed invariant is a complete all-parameter distribution requiring a nontrivial torus character count plus affine boundary stratification. The \(q=2\) degeneracy is explicitly classified.
